Axiom:
Phase cannot emit Handoff without one successful `sdd-verify --task --phase `. The SDD facade, not the phase agent, freezes scope/rules/selector, invokes the universal Verify engine once, and atomically terminalizes its runner-owned attempt evidence from the exact `VerifyRunReport`. Failed, blocked, interrupted, timed-out, cancelled, environment-failed and violation attempts remain in append-only history; the phase stays `[~] IN_PROGRESS` until resolved or escalated.
**MANDATORY (PROTOCOL) — Canonical Gate Rule:** The ticket kind resolves one composed selector and the preset/config owns its steps; the agent never chooses or substitutes individual gates. Diagnostics may run while fixing, but only the canonical phase command can create completion evidence; a hand-written `ver` line is not evidence. A frozen legacy receipt is produced only by an explicitly provenance-bearing compatibility overlay whose commands bind exactly before spawn; it is never the no-overlay default.
The canon covers the script's BODY, not just its name in §5. Editing what a §5 script actually runs (e.g. rewriting `"typecheck"` in `package.json` so it does less, or points elsewhere) while logging the unchanged §5 command name is the same violation — the command stayed canonical on paper while its behavior was substituted underneath it. The one exception: `package.json` (or the script body) is itself among this phase's Target Files AND the change to that script IS the phase's stated Objective (a `bootstrap` / `config` phase whose job is exactly to define or rewire the script) — then the edit is legitimate work, not a gate dodge, and MUST be recorded as its own decision line in the Execution Log (` decision rewritten ← `) before the gate runs.
`sdd-verify --task --phase ` is NOT supplemental — it owns STEP_5 through the same Verify planner/runner as standalone `verify` (see `AX_PERMITTED_BASH_COMMANDS`). The ticket does not copy a static gate ladder and never repeats `sdd-verify`.
Phase kind `doc` typically has no verification — empty section is acceptable.
